policy: Michael is the archangel, as Jude calls him (JUD 1:9), and Gabriel is an angel, as Luke and Daniel call him; that tradition counts Gabriel among the archangels is said on his record as tradition, not as the text.
source: Essenthos, on the project owner's decision of 2026-10-25 that Michael is the archangel and Gabriel an angel, as the text calls them

says.notes: Daniel calls him 'one of the chief princes' (DAN 10:13), 'Michael your prince' (DAN 10:21) and 'the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people' (DAN 12:1). Jude calls him 'Michael the archangel', who contended with the devil about the body of Moses (JUD 1:9), and in Revelation 'Michael and his angels' fight against the dragon (REV 12:7). He is the only archangel the text names.

rulings.why: 'Yet Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil': the archangel of Daniel's visions and of Revelation 12.

says.notes: Gabriel is named four times. In Daniel he is sent to make Daniel understand the vision (DAN 8:16), and 'the man Gabriel' comes to him about the time of the evening oblation (DAN 9:21). In Luke he is the angel of the Lord who appeared to Zacharias (LUK 1:11) and said 'I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God' (LUK 1:19), and the angel sent from God to Mary in Nazareth (LUK 1:26). Tradition counts him among the archangels; the text calls him an angel, and the only archangel it names is Michael (JUD 1:9).

rulings.why: 'I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of God': the angel sent to Zacharias and to Mary, whom Daniel saw.
